default.text: Every house we design starts with the same drawing: a section through the stair, at 1:20, in pencil. Before the plan, before the facade, before anyone has asked how many bedrooms there will be.
default.note: The habit comes from Ingrid Holm's years in a joinery workshop in Bergen, where stairs were built before the walls around them.

default.text: A stair decides how a family meets. Put it by the front door and people pass each other all day. Hide it at the back and the upper floor becomes a separate country.
default.note: In the Fjellveien house the landing is wide enough for a reading chair. It is the most used seat in the building.

default.text: It also sets the budget for daylight. A stair that is open to the roof carries light two floors down, which is worth more to us than a larger window that faces the neighbour.
So when clients ask what to bring to the first meeting, we say: a list of who gets up first in the morning, and where they go.
default.note: Most lists are shorter than people expect. The record so far is four lines.
